input: # What `reading: 'spec'` gives where it parts from the base grammars'
# reading. Only the TypeScript package has this option yet, so these rows
# are here and not in ../spec/ (see ../AGENTS.md, "Where a new fixture
# goes"). ../spec/raw-yaml-scalars.tsv pins the base reading of the same
# A comment starts with # and nothing else. // and /* */ are text.
# A # after white space still starts one.
# A number is one the YAML core schema reads as a number: a decimal
# integer or float with an optional sign, 0o octal and 0x hexadecimal.
# Anything else is the text as written: an underscore, a binary
# integer, an upper-case prefix, a sign before a prefix, and the words
# JavaScript has for the values that are not finite.
# With text after it, a number was text already.
# A member name is the text as written, under both readings.
# A quoted scalar is a string, as ever.
# JSON text reads the same on both paths: its numbers are core numbers.
# An empty document after the description is passed over: a marker with
# nothing after it, with a comment after it, or with a marker after it.
# A second document that holds anything is still refused, null written
# out included, and so is a description that comes second.
# The root is still checked: a list first and nothing after is a list.
# The words of YAML 1.1 are the yaml grammar's to read, and it reads
# them as booleans under both readings until it offers the choice. A
# The core schema's own words are unchanged.
